title: Cartesian comparison of residue fibres with flat horizontal projections
statement: Let $S,X,Y,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$, $f:X\to Y$, $h:T\to S$ morphisms satisfying $q\circ f=p$. Set $X_T=X\times_ST$, $Y_T=Y\times_ST$ with projections $\pi_X,\pi_Y,p_T,q_T$, and let $f_T:X_T\to Y_T$ be induced by $f$ and $\mathrm{id}_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For $t\in T$ and $s=h(t)$, let $r:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ be the induced residue-field homomorphism [def-weil-residue-field], and put $e=\operatorname{Spec}(r):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There are canonical isomorphisms $(X_T)_t\cong X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $(Y_T)_t\cong Y_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Write $a:(X_T)_t\to X_s$ and $b:(Y_T)_t\to Y_s$ for the first projections under these isomorphisms. They satisfy $f_s\circ a=b\circ(f_T)_t$, and the square with horizontal maps $a,b$ and vertical maps $(f_T)_t,f_s$ is cartesian. If $\iota_s:X_s\to X$ and $\iota'_t:(X_T)_t\to X_T$ are fibre inclusions, then $\iota_s\circ a=\pi_X\circ\iota'_t$, and the analogous identity holds for $Y$. The morphisms $e,a,b$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. No finite-type, finite-presentation, flatness, or Noetherian hypothesis on $p,q,f,h$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, lemma-base-change-criterion-flatness-fibre, proof final displayed cartesian fibre square and the following sentence asserting flatness of its horizontal arrows. Canonical projection compatibility and flatness of the residue-field extension are included.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] to $(p,h,t)$ and $(q,h,t)$. Write $K=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $L=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, $A=(X_T)_t$, $B=(Y_T)_t$, and $\rho_X:A\to L$, $\rho_Y:B\to L$ for their structure maps. It gives the canonical identifications $A\cong X_s\times_K L$, $B\cong Y_s\times_K L$ with first projections $a,b$, and gives exactly $\iota_s a=\pi_X\iota'_t$ and its $Y$ analogue. In particular $a,b$ are base changes of $e:L\to K$.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, lemma-base-change-criterion-flatness-fibre, final cartesian diagram and its following sentence; expansion of the canonical maps by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: Here is the universal-property check of the square [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Put $F=(f_T)_t$. By the definition of the induced fibre map, $\rho_YF=\rho_X$. The two maps $f_sa,bF:A\to Y_s$ have the same composites to $Y$, namely $f\pi_X\iota'_t$, and to $K$, namely $e\rho_X$; hence they are equal. To prove cartesianness, let $D$ be any scheme with $u:D\to X_s$ and $v:D\to B$ satisfying $f_su=bv$. Set $\ell=\rho_Yv$. If $k_X:X_s\to K$ and $k_Y:Y_s\to K$ are the structure maps, then $k_Xu=k_Yf_su=k_Ybv=e\ell$. The universal property of $A=X_s\times_K L$ gives a unique $w:D\to A$ with $aw=u$ and $\rho_Xw=\ell$. Now $Fw$ and $v$ have the same composites with $b$ and $\rho_Y$, so the universal property of $B=Y_s\times_K L$ gives $Fw=v$. Any other lift has the same $a$-projection and, because $\rho_YF=\rho_X$, the same $L$-projection; thus it equals $w$. This is the required cartesian universal property.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, lemma-base-change-criterion-flatness-fibre, final cartesian diagram and its following sentence; expansion of the canonical maps by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: The residue-field map $r:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ makes $\kappa(t)$ a field extension of $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. By [lem-pc-field-extension-flat], $e=\operatorname{Spec}(r)$ is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] applied to the two cartesian identifications of step 1, its base changes $a$ and $b$ are flat. All three cited statements allow arbitrary field extensions and arbitrary parameter morphisms; no finiteness or flatness hypothesis on $p,q,f,h$ was used.
